newsitem.title: USA: GMAC acquires LSI Holdings, forms subprime unit.
newsitem.headline: GMAC acquires LSI Holdings, forms subprime unit.

text.p: General Motors Acceptance Corp said Tuesday it will enter the "subprime" auto lending business with its acquisition of LSI Holdings Inc, a subprime financing and servicing firm based in Little Rock, Ark.
GMAC, the finance arm of General Motors Corp, said LSI will form the basis for a new GMAC subsidiary, Nuvell Credit Corp, which will conduct operations as a stand-alone finance unit.
Subprime lending goes to higher-risk borrowers who normally would not qualify for auto loans from banks or major credit firms.
Nuvell is expected to begin operations within the next 60 days in Georgia and Illinois with a small number of GM dealers who have successful experience in subprime financing.
Terms of the deal to acquire LSI were not disclosed. The company's chairman, Tim Sambrano, will become president of Nuvell, which will be based at LSI's Little Rock headquarters.
The move by GMAC, one of the world's largest finance companies, to get into the U.S. subprime auto lending business comes at a time of turmoil in the $50-$70 billion industry.

In July, Deerfield, Ill.-based First Merchants Acceptance Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection after defaulting on its bank loan agreements and finding accounting irregularities "involving unauthorized entries" in its records.

Dallas-based Jayhawk Acceptance also has filed for bankruptcy protection, while Deerfield, Ill.-based Mercury Finance Co was forced to restate its earnings for four years due to accounting irregularities.
Despite the trouble, GMAC said it sees profits in subprime financing.

"GMAC's entry into subprime financing is consistent with our long-range plans to profitably expand our involvement in the financial services industry," said John Rines, GMAC president. "Through Nuvell we're looking to grow our business and to gain a profitable share of a very sizable automotive financing segment."
